summary: The candidate corrects abort-only sanitization for FP32 and consolidates cache/backend cleanup, but FP16 full-NaN rows still become all -inf and produce NaN softmax values before host-side request abort processing.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded base reproduced uniform 163840-way sampling after sanitizing a full-NaN GPU row (p=6.1035157e-06); base lacks SGLANG_ABORT_ON_NAN_LOGITS, causing the final probe to raise AttributeError.
Candidate regression suite: 6 passed, including FP32 abort-only sanitization and request marking.
9 tests and 2 subtests passed; mocked comprehensive cleanup hooks were exercised.
Existing sampling-mask regression suite passed (with skips reported by the suite).

tests.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 prepared-python inline dtype adversarial probe
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X, FP32 and BF16 abort-only rows became finite, but FP16 remained non-finite and softmax returned NaN. Full-row detection correctly distinguished a partial-NaN row.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, ROCm/HIP 7.2.26015; real GPU tensors tested for float32, float16, and bfloat16.

remaining_counterexamples: With SGLANG_ABORT_ON_NAN_LOGITS=1 and SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=0, a fully-NaN FP16 GPU row is replaced by all -inf because -1e30 is outside FP16 range; softmax is still NaN before request-scoped abort processing.
Speculative decoding with a full-NaN mask still raises an assertion instead of performing request-scoped containment.
Hierarchical-cache write-through safety has mocked cleanup coverage but no live hierarchical-cache regression, so poisoned host-cache publication is not end-to-end verified.
remaining_limitations: No Blackwell SM10x or Kimi-K3 weights/TP=8 environment was available; the qualified claim is limited to an MI350X numerical fixture and unit-level scheduler processing.
No live hierarchical-cache, multimodal, disaggregated-offload, HiSparse, or multi-node serving deployment was available.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate changes only Python, documentation, tests, and reports.
